summary: Crash and/or data corruption upon attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks
description: The bug Attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks causes the player to be unable to respawn. The game crashes (Exception generating new chunk caused by java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and/or the world is corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), and you become unable to open it again. "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" is spammed to the debug log. To reproduce 1. Create a new world. 2. Execute /worldborder center 50000000 50000000. 3. Execute /kill. 4. You are unable to respawn. 5. Attempt to go to title screen. 6. The game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new world.
3. Execute the command `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`.
4. Execute the command `/kill`.
5. Observe that you are unable to respawn.
6. Attempt to go to the title screen.
7. Observe that the game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center set over 30 million blocks, the player experiences a critical failure that prevents them from respawning. The game crashes with an error message indicating an exception generated by new chunk creation, specifically a java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. In some instances, this action leads to world corruption, resulting in a java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException, which subsequently makes the world inaccessible. The debug log repeatedly displays the message "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)," indicating a recurring issue related to the crash. To reproduce this bug, one must create a new world, then execute the command to set the world border center at coordinates 50,000,000 by 50,000,000. Following this, executing the /kill command results in an inability to respawn. Attempting to return to the title screen leads to either a game crash or the world becoming permanently unopenable.
Expected Behavior: When a player attempts to save a world with a world border center set over 30 million blocks, the game should allow the player to respawn normally after executing the /kill command. The world should save without any issues, and the player should be able to return to the title screen without experiencing crashes or data corruption. The game should function as expected, without any errors logged in the debug log.
